title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 54 (Issue of Sweat Equity Shares)

content.overview: Section 54 permits a company to issue sweat equity shares of a class of shares already issued, to its directors or employees, at a discount or for consideration other than cash, for providing know-how or making available rights in the nature of intellectual property or value additions, subject to a special resolution and prescribed conditions including valuation, limits and lock-in.
content.glance: Sweat equity to directors/employees for know-how/IP/value additions; special resolution; prescribed conditions; exception to the discount ban under s. 53.
content.study: Notwithstanding anything contained in section 53, a company may issue sweat equity shares of a class of shares already issued if the issue is authorised by a special resolution; the resolution specifies the number of shares, current market price, consideration (if any) and the class of directors or employees to whom they are issued; not less than one year has elapsed since the date on which the company became entitled to commence business; and the sweat equity shares are issued in accordance with prescribed regulations on valuation, limits, lock-in and other conditions. ‘Sweat equity shares’ means equity shares issued at a discount or for consideration other than cash for providing know-how or making available rights in the nature of intellectual property or value additions. Current-law framing: confirm special resolution and eligibility; apply prescribed conditions; treat as exception to s. 53.

sections.heading: Meaning and purpose
sections.body: Sweat equity shares are equity shares of a class already issued, issued to directors or employees at a discount or for non-cash consideration for providing know-how, making available intellectual-property rights or value additions.

sections.heading: Special resolution and particulars
sections.body: The issue requires a special resolution specifying the number of shares, current market price, consideration (if any) and class of directors or employees to whom shares are issued.

sections.heading: One-year condition
sections.body: At least one year must have elapsed since the company became entitled to commence business.

sections.heading: Prescribed conditions
sections.body: The issue must comply with prescribed requirements, including valuation, limits, lock-in and other applicable conditions. Check the current Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules for the exact requirements.

sections.heading: Relationship with section 53
sections.body: Section 54 operates notwithstanding the general prohibition on issue of shares at a discount in section 53; it is a controlled exception, not a general permission for discounted employee shares.

examples.title: Compliant sweat equity
examples.body: After a special resolution and valuation, a company issues sweat equity to an employee for IP contributed. Section 54 is complied with; s. 53 does not void the issue.

examples.title: Missing special resolution
examples.body: Sweat equity is issued without a special resolution. Section 54 conditions are not met.

hypotheticals.question: Is sweat equity free of all capital rules?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It is a regulated exception to s. 53 and must satisfy special resolution, eligibility, valuation and prescribed conditions under s. 54.

distinctions.title: Sweat equity (s. 54) vs discount prohibition (s. 53)
distinctions.left: Regulated exception for directors/employees for know-how/IP

misconceptions.trap: Any discounted issue to employees is automatically valid as sweat equity.
misconceptions.correction: Sweat equity requires special resolution, prescribed conditions and a qualifying purpose (know-how/IP/value additions).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What makes an issue qualify as sweat equity?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It must meet the statutory definition and be issued to eligible directors/employees for qualifying know-how, intellectual-property rights or value additions, with the required resolution and prescribed conditions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does section 54 remove all restrictions on discounted shares?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. It creates a limited route subject to special resolution, the one-year condition and prescribed requirements.
